label: TP-Link TL-SG2008P
description: 8-port gigabit JetStream smart switch with PoE+: 8x 10/100/1000 RJ45, 802.3af/at on ports 1-4 and a 62 W PoE budget.
notes: Vendor figures from the TP-Link datasheet: interface is 8x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45 ports (ports 1-4 support 802.3at/af PoE+), auto negotiation / auto MDI/MDIX; PoE standard 802.3af/at on ports 1-4 against a 62 W budget (the vendor's 62 W is the PD-side allowance - its max-consumption row reads 77.3 W with 62 W of PD attached - so it is recorded in poe.budgetW, not left as prose). Half the row is PoE and half is not, which is what the port model shows; ports 5-8 are declared poeOut:false because engine/media.js fills a silent poeOut on every RJ45 port of a switch that claims poe-pse, and the silence was producing four invented 15.4 W PSE ports that then drew on the 62 W budget. The page moved from tp-link.com to omadanetworks.com when the line was rebranded, and this SKU is now marked End of Sale there with the SG2008P as its successor (modelled at devices/tp-link/SG2008P.json); the port census and the 62 W budget are the same on both pages.

poe.note: Vendor table, row "PoE Ports (RJ45)": "Standard: 802.3af/at compliant / PoE Ports: 4 Ports / Power Supply: 62 W*" (https://www.omadanetworks.com/us/business-networking/omada-switch-access/tl-sg2008p/, HTTP 200, 187,036 B, read 2026-11-21; the tp-link.com path for this SKU now 301s here). The 62 W is what the PoE ports may deliver, not the adapter's rating: the adapter is 53.5 V DC / 1.31 A (70.1 W) and the V3 max-consumption row is "77.3 W (110 V/60 Hz) (with 62 W PD connected)" - 62 W of PD load plus ~15 W of chassis. Four 802.3af loads (61.6 W) fit; four class-4 25.5 W loads (102 W) do not.
